en: Old temple, an osmanthus tree
Dusk slowly rises
Fine rain, the shadow of an umbrella arriving late
Confucius said: to know what one knows
To know that you do not know is true knowledge
Summer cicada song: I know, I know

points.zh:
“as we know, there are known knowns; there are things we know we know. We also know there are known unknowns we know there are some things we do not know. But there are also unknown unknowns-- the ones we don’t know we don’t know.”
--Donald Rumsfeld, United States Secretary of Defense. （2002）

en: There is always a stretch of lake water
One can hoist the cloud-sail straight, and follow
Fan Li, vanishing into the hazy mist

points.zh: 范蠡（又名陶朱公）是越王勾踐成功復國的謀士和功臣，春秋時期著名的政治家，也是一名出色的商人。為人博學多才，謙遜有禮，懂得明哲保身，深受好評。 世人贊其“ 智以保身，商以致富，忠以爲國 ”。傳説，范蠡幫越王勾踐滅吴王夫差，雪耻復國後，功成身退，帶走西施，隱居於太湖的迷濛雲煙。
points.en: Fan Li (also known as Tao Zhu Gong) was the strategist and meritorious statesman who helped King Goujian of Yue successfully restore his kingdom — a renowned statesman of the Spring and Autumn period and also an accomplished merchant. Learned and versatile, modest and courteous, he understood how to preserve himself wisely, and was widely praised. People of his time praised him: "wise enough to preserve himself, skilled in commerce enough to grow rich, loyal enough to serve his country." Legend has it that after Fan Li helped King Goujian of Yue destroy King Fuchai of Wu and avenge his humiliation by restoring the kingdom, he retired at the height of his success, took Xi Shi away with him, and lived in seclusion amid the misty clouds of Lake Tai.

en: Packing a bag of the Ganges' evening glow
Coming home, unfolding
Incense smoke curling upward

flow.caption_zh: 印度教聖地Varanasi。  恆河岸邊黄昏的梵煙

points.zh: Varanasi (瓦拉納西) 位於恆河岸邊的中等城市，卻保留著1500多座寺廟，每年有400多個宗敎節日。公元前五世紀佛祖釋迦牟尼在這裡傳敎，公元七世紀中國唐代高僧玄奘到此朝拜取經。十―世紀穆斯林佔領此地直到十八世紀，其間建立了許多清真寺。不過瓦拉納西還是因印度教而聲名遠播。飲恆河水，敬濕婆神，結交聖人，住瓦拉納西，是印度敎徒一生最大的願望。百分之八十以上的印度人是印度敎徒，瓦拉納西是濕婆神的領地，是印度敎徒的聖地。
points.en: Located in a medium-sized city on the banks of the Ganges River, Varanasi has more than 1,500 temples and more than 400 festivals every year. The Buddha Shakyamuni preached here in the 5th century BC, and the high priest Xuanzheng of the Tang Dynasty in China came here in the 7th century AD to worship and learn the Sutras. Tenth-century Muslims occupied the area until the eighteenth century, during which many mosques were built. Still, Varanasi was famous for its Hinduism. Drinking Ganges water, paying homage to Shiva, making friends with saints, and living in Varanasi are the greatest wishes of the Hindus in their lifetime. More than 80% of Indians are Hindustani, and Varanasi is the territory of Shiva, the holy place of Hindustani.

en: In winter, white snow falling thick
Whatever path one takes, it is always possible
Meeting the fisherman who angles alone on the cold river

zh: 踏出，歷史的紛繁和滄桑
en: Because it bears a beautiful name
Dadaocheng, where mottled old streets remain
Stepping out into history's tangled complexity and change

points.zh: 大稻埕，是臺北市大同區西南部的一個傳統地域名稱，因具有大片曬稻穀的空地（稻埕）而得名。咸豐元年（1851年）泉州府同安縣人林藍田為躲避海盜洗劫，自雞籠（今基隆）遷至大稻埕經商並開設店鋪，開始了大稻埕的商業活動。1853年 三邑人與同安人為艋舺碼頭的泊船權利，發生頂下郊拚分類械鬥事件，下郊的同安人無力抵抗，於是帶著自身信仰的霞海城隍敗逃至大稻埕。大稻埕旁淡水河的碼頭交易逐漸興起。1860年淡水開港後，大稻埕成為臺北最繁華的物資集散中心，以茶葉與布料的貿易為主。大稻埕的茶葉貿易在洋行的帶領下，不僅市場擴大，更造就驚人的財富與繁榮。進入日治時期後日商抵制洋行勢力，轉而以日本與東南亞為主要市場。戰後大稻埕因淡水河淤淺逐漸失去河港功能，且臺產茶葉不敵錫蘭紅茶的競爭而逐漸沒落。之後臺北市區逐漸向東發展，人口大量外移，大稻埕逐成為臺北市外圍的老舊市區。              （ 維基百科 ）
points.en: Dadaocheng is a traditional place name for the southwestern part of Taipei's Datong District, named for the large flat area once used for drying rice (稻埕, "rice-drying yard"). In the first year of the Xianfeng era (1851), Lin Lantian, a native of Tong'an County in Quanzhou Prefecture, moved from Jilong (present-day Keelung) to Dadaocheng to escape pirate raids, and set up shop there, beginning Dadaocheng's commercial activity. In 1853, the Sanyi people and the Tong'an people fought the "Dingxia Jiao Pin" factional feud over mooring rights at Bangka wharf; the Tong'an people of Xiajiao, unable to resist, fled to Dadaocheng carrying their Xiahai City God temple's deity with them. Trade at the wharves along the Tamsui River next to Dadaocheng gradually flourished. After the opening of the Tamsui port in 1860, Dadaocheng became Taipei's most prosperous center for the distribution of goods, mainly trading in tea and cloth. Dadaocheng's tea trade, led by foreign trading houses, not only expanded in market size but also created astonishing wealth and prosperity. Entering the Japanese colonial period, Japanese merchants pushed back against the foreign trading houses' influence, shifting their main markets toward Japan and Southeast Asia instead. After the war, Dadaocheng gradually lost its function as a river port as the Tamsui River silted up, and Taiwanese tea, unable to compete with Ceylon black tea, gradually declined. Afterward, Taipei's urban area gradually developed eastward, the population moved out in large numbers, and Dadaocheng became an old, peripheral district of the city. (Wikipedia)

flow.caption_zh: 台灣膠彩畫大師郭雪湖著名作品〈南街殷賑〉將30年代大稻埕的繁華景觀展現無遺。
2014年葉天倫執導的電影「大稻埕」，回顧 大稻埕的歷史和當時的繁榮與進步。

en: Those uneven, scattered fragments
Those rises and falls
Turning into life's refrain
That year, a few promises were left behind
Looking back again, there is no wind or rain either
Nor is it clear?

zh: 天涯可流浪，海角可期望？
en: After the rain, a song rises like wind, asking
Over the Rainbow, is there
Can one wander to the edge of the sky, can one hope at the corner of the sea?

flow.caption_zh: 日本深浦海岸不老不死温泉海邊晨景

points.zh:
《 Over the Rainbow 》is a ballad composed by Harold Arlen with lyrics by E.Y. Harburg. It was written for the movie “The Wizard of Oz” and was sung by actress Judy Garland in her starring role as Dorothy Gale. It won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and became Garland's signature song.
Somewhere over the rainbow
Way up high
And the dreams that you dream of
Once in a lullaby
Somewhere over the rainbow
Bluebirds fly
And the dreams that you dream of
Dreams really do come true
Someday, I wish upon a star
Wake up where the clouds are far behind me
Where trouble melts like lemon drops
High above the chimney top
That's where you'll find me
Somewhere over the rainbow
Bluebirds fly
And the dreams that you dare to
Oh why, oh why can't I ?
